summary: Ottawa and Stellantis meet in Toronto over the Brampton plant as reports dispute the government's role, and Carney joins European leaders in Dublin.
body: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly was due to meet Stellantis, the Unifor union and Ontario's economic development minister Vic Fedeli in Toronto on Thursday about the carmaker's plan to sell its idle Brampton plant to armoured-vehicle maker Roshel.[^1][^2] Her office says the government "has no choice" but to find Stellantis in default of the conditions attached to up to $529 million in federal support promised in 2022.[^2] Roshel says it may rehire some of the roughly 2,000 laid-off workers, and the sale is expected to close by year-end.[^2]

The government's own role is now in question. CTV News, citing three unnamed sources, reported that Ottawa was "actively and intensively part" of the talks and met the companies more than a dozen times; CBC reported the government knew for months.[^2][^3] Joly's office calls the claim that she was involved in the Roshel deal "false" and says she only tried to settle the dispute between Stellantis and Unifor.[^2] Unifor's Lana Payne called the sale a "worst-case scenario".[^1]

Abroad, Prime Minister Mark Carney is in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, where Canada is the only non-European country taking part, before heading on to summits in Asia. He also meets the leaders of Greece and Cyprus, two countries that have not yet ratified Canada's trade deal with the EU.[^1] At home, heavy rain has forced evacuations around Pemberton on B.C.'s south coast.[^1]
differences: Unnamed sources told CTV that Ottawa took an active part in the talks that led to the sale and did not block it.[^3] Joly's office says the government never backed a Roshel deal and that reports of her involvement are false.[^2][^3]

reads.title: Joly didn't meet with Roshel before deal signed with Stellantis: minister's office
reads.summary: Sets out both sides of the dispute over what Ottawa knew about the Brampton sale, and what the $529 million in federal support was for.
